extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental investigators, and students of scientific method
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive method for discovering 'forms' (laws) by collecting instances, constructing comparative and exclusive tables, and deriving affirmative definitions—illustrated by the investigation of heat. Guidance is aimed at experimental philosophers designing and interpreting experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Degrees / Comparative Instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble a table that orders bodies and phenomena by degrees of the quality under investigation (e.g., potential vs. actual heat; bodies not warm, those with latent heat, those warm to touch, varieties and strengths of flame).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List many instances across categories (inanimate bodies, vegetables, animals, heavenly bodies, ignited substances, motion effects, etc.), note doubtful traditions, and annotate with 'Let the experiment be tried' where historical reports are uncertain. Use the table to observe what increases or decreases with the given nature and to find comparative limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present a comprehensive review of instances before induction
rubrics_metrics.description: Before drawing conclusions, present a review of collected instances to the understanding so the investigator can search for a nature always present/absent with the given nature and which increases or decreases with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review is preparatory: induction acts only after the instances are surveyed. Avoid jumping to axioms from incomplete instance-sets; note provenance and reliability of instances and prefer experimental confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceed from negatives (exclusions) to affirmatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin by rejecting candidate natures that cannot be the true form (exclusive method), and only after exclusion should one attempt to assert the affirmative form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection is primary because human minds tend to create premature affirmative hypotheses. Use contradictory instances to destroy hypotheses; every single contradictory instance can suffice to reject a proposed nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive Table (rejection of natures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a table of natures to be rejected for the form in question, citing instances that contradict each candidate nature (e.g., reject 'elementary', 'celestial', 'rarity', 'imparting of substance', 'flame or light' as the form of heat, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each proposed nature, provide specific contrary instances that show it cannot be the form (the text gives many: sun's rays, subterranean fires, ignited metals, thermometric expansion, frictional heat, etc.). Use these exclusions to free the mind from misleading traditional hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: First vintage / liberty of the understanding (tentative affirmative)
rubrics_metrics.description: After composing the preparatory tables and exclusions, allow the mind to attempt a first affirmative interpretation (a tentative 'first vintage') of the form based on conspicuous instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a provisional, interpretive stage. The affirmative arrived at here is subject to further checks, corrections, and stronger induction; look for conspicuous ('coruscation') instances where the form is least obscured by other natures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form must be inherent and universal in instances
rubrics_metrics.description: A true form (definition/law) must be inherent in every individual instance of the thing; no genuine contradictory instance can exist if the form is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for the element that is present in all cases where the nature occurs and absent where it does not. Use conspicuous instances to make the form more evident and test the form across heterogeneous cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek conspicuous (coruscation) and solitary instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Use conspicuous instances—cases where the candidate form is less restrained by other natures—and solitary instances—cases that share nothing with other subjects except the nature under investigation—to accelerate exclusion and confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solitary instances (e.g., prisms, crystalline gems for color) are powerful because they isolate the nature. Prefer instances that minimize confounding factors to make the form clearer with fewer examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish form from mere communication or sensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate the true form (the law or nature) from the phenomena of communication (e.g., heating by contact) and from sensible effects relative to the senses (sensible heat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate the ability of a body to heat another (transmission) or the sensory feeling of warmth with the essential form. Recognize sensible heat as a relation to animal spirit rather than the absolute form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/experimental test for a candidate form
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an operational criterion: if one can excite the proposed fundamental motion or condition (e.g., an expansive motion partly repressed) and thereby produce the phenomenon across diverse substances, this supports the candidate form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test should be applicable to any susceptible substance (animal, vegetable, mineral, air, oil, water, etc.). Use experiments that deliberately induce the hypothesized operative condition and observe whether the target phenomenon (heat) results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four specific differences limiting 'motion' as the form of heat
rubrics_metrics.description: If motion is proposed as the genus of heat, it must be limited by particular differences: (I) expansive motion, (II) expansion with upward tendency, (III) motion of small particles restrained and alternating, (IV) rapid stimulation in particles of tolerable size (not the sluggish action of time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple lines of evidence (flame and boiling liquids, thermometric behavior, effects of pressure, frictional heating, differences between slow chemical/temporal processes and violent heat, behavior of air, mercury, metals, etc.) to test each difference. These four limitations together define the candidate form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experimental checks (explicitly 'Let the experiment be tried')
rubrics_metrics.description: Where historical reports or inferred instances are uncertain, explicitly perform experiments to confirm or refute those instances and the hypotheses drawn from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly annotates doubtful reports and prescribes direct experimentation (e.g., tests with burning-glasses, thermometers, compression of burning bodies, rods with cold applied above/below). Empirical trial is integral at every stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid traditional/abstract forms; define forms as operative laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject vague traditional or metaphysical 'forms' (concrete or abstract ideas) and instead treat a form as the law or rule of simple action that arranges a simple nature (e.g., heat, light, weight) in susceptible subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground definitions in observable operative differences and laws; do not rely on medieval or scholastic abstractions. Treat 'form of X' as the functional law governing X's behavior across instances.
